title: Two kinds of thought, and what words cannot hold

lectures.id: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3
Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

overview: Chapter 40 continues the study of *machshava*, thought, and sorts it into two kinds. The first is the thought of *ratzon*, desire. Desire is clothed at once in the thought of the mind, so the two are one, and this thought is hidden and subconscious. It arrives in the fine nerves of the brain as a simple thought, without letters, and moves the limbs before a person is aware of it. The second is the thought of *sechel*, understanding, which is made of letters. *Bina* grasps an idea, makes distinctions and gives them names and symbols, as in the example of drawing a face. Understanding comes before words, and *Leah* is words thought without the understanding behind them. Inside *bina* there is a depth of the concept that words cannot hold, and that depth is also the essence of the *Torah*. Both kinds of thought run through every level of the *seder hishtalshelus*, and both come from the essence of the soul. The chapter ends with the revelation of *Keser* in *Bina*, the *Atik* revealed in *Bina*, and the three points of the letter *yud*.

sections.title: Desire moves the limbs before we are aware of it
sections.summary: Desire is not clothed in letters. It arrives in the fine nerves of the brain as a simple, spontaneous thought, and it moves the limbs before a person is aware of wanting to move them. The rest of the section compares this with conscious thought and asks how the two are to work together.

blocks.text: Desire is only in the very fine nerves, which carry the power of movement and feeling to the limbs; there the power and light of desire are expressed, and the limbs listen to the desire in the mind.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: Lifting a hand or foot, or drawing it back, is done only by the desire that rises in the mind, before a person has told himself what he is doing. Walking, or talking with the hands, is not thought out step by step; it just happens. This is called subconscious, or spontaneous: no premeditation, you know what you want and how to do it.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: If a person has a stroke, G-d forbid, and must relearn walking and speech, the intellect can help: a coach can talk him through the practice. But the aim is unconscious competence; talking oneself through the motions does not work functionally.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: Even in relearning the desire knows what it wants; its letters must be reimprinted in a new part of the brain. It keeps sending its message, but it does not get across: it must go through the physical body.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: A person is asked to push a button to light a lamp whenever he wants, with his brain hooked to monitors. Watchers can tell a second before the push, by what is called an action potential: the desire already shows as real letters, subconscious, before he is aware of it.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: Conscious thought can monitor and coach itself; that leads to learning and *hisbonenus*, which unlocks the *omek*, the *Keser*, and gets back to the desire higher than understanding. For now he makes only the basic distinction.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: Today's culture has a lot of materialism in science, reducing human psychology to physical things. They like to point to this experiment and say you have no free choice, since the monitors know what you will do first. But the conscious sense of knowing what you want, he thinks, comes from something deeper: the inner *ratzon*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

sensitivity.reason: Criticises how scientists and a materialist culture read this experiment. A criticism of a way of thinking, kept as said; the public text names no one.
sensitivity.publishable: Today's culture has a lot of materialism, reducing human psychology to physical things. Some people like to point to this experiment and say you have no free choice, since the monitors know what you will do first. But the conscious sense of knowing what you want, he thinks, comes from something deeper: the inner *ratzon*.

blocks.text: The narration 'now I want to do this' comes after the true desire, so the experiment says nothing about choice. The monitors see the letters of desire but cannot predict when a person will act. What it shows is that our conscious self is not our whole self.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: A key idea of *Chassidus*, as in chapters 5 and 6: there is *yesh*, the tangible things we can know, and *ayin*. The conscious self is only a small part of who we are; most of reality is the *makif* level, *sovev kol almin*, beyond what we can understand.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: We often make the mistake of thinking that what we can measure matters more than what we cannot. In scientific data and decision making there is a bias to focus on what is easy to quantify, even when it is not the only factor, or the most important one.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

sensitivity.reason: Criticises how scientists weigh data in decisions. A criticism of method, kept as said.
sensitivity.publishable: We often make the mistake of thinking that what we can measure matters more than what we cannot. In data and decision making there is a bias to focus on what is easy to quantify, even when it is not the only factor, or the most important one.

blocks.text: The same is true of ourselves: much of our motivation is deeper than the conscious part. *Kuntres HaHispaalus* speaks of the inner connection our G-dly soul has, much deeper than any *hispaalus* or understanding: it is our essence.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: Learn to separate the two. Nobody fully understands the essence of our soul, a piece of G-d, but that is who we are. Our experiences of these things are not rational and cannot be logically quantified. He compares it to walking: he does not walk by logic, he just does, and the same with talking.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: People have written books about the two ways the brain thinks, one fast and one slow. Many things we do need to be done in the subconscious way; at other times it helps to stop, analyze, filter and coach oneself. We need the interplay between both.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: Is it better to think, or to do naturally what the subconscious wants? The answer is yes, you need both: the conscious part trains us, unlocks these things and channels them into *kelim*, which is essential for *tikkun*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: Doing only what is natural is very powerful, but it is *tohu*, which has too much light for its vessels. Doing only what is rational is *tikkun*: strong vessels, weak lights, missing the power beyond understanding.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: The task is to bring the lights of *tohu* into the vessels of *tikkun*: take things like *mesiras nefesh* and *emunah*, which are beyond understanding, and build a framework, with humility and openness, in which one can recognize and channel them, being comfortable with what one does not know (*bitachon*). That is bringing *Moshiach*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: On a personal level this is the right harmony: conscious thought alone stifles a person; subconscious thought alone is a little kid running around without a diaper. There needs to be training and filtering.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

phrases.he: (בלשון אידיש פאר שטאנד) שבא מיד בעיון המחשבה
phrases.en: so that right away is expressed in analysis

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

phrases.en: and this is the power of the intellectual, analytical thought

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

phrases.en: that it's able to be a *kli* to contain any sort of analysis, any intellectual idea

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

phrases.en: and this kind of *machshava* doesn't have *ratzon* in it

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: Any idea or logic grasped in the mind, which we call understanding, is expressed right away in analysis, where a mental framework of words is built. That is what *bina* does: it makes distinctions.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: *Bina* also throws things away: there is far too much data, so we filter out the important features.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.title: Drawing a face
blocks.text: He points to a book on drawing, *Drawing on the Right Side of the Brain*, which speaks of the difference between *chachma* and *bina*, the right and left sides of the brain. Asked to draw a face, most people draw a symbol for each named part: an eye, a nose. The forehead comes out much too small, the back of the head is cut down, and the proportions are off. The drawing is flat, like an Egyptian hieroglyph, and the eye faces the wrong way.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: That is both the strength and the flaw of *bina*: it takes the rich reality, picks the important parts, and gives them names and symbols; experts do the same with jargon. To draw properly one must draw exactly what one sees, including what has no name: the abstract shadows and differences of light and dark. That is the skill of drawing, and of art in general: a framework that can channel what is beyond what we can name.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: *Machshava iyunis* is the power to hold any intellectual analysis, with no *ratzon* in it at all: only the ability to create logical structures and systems.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

phrases.he: ולא נקרא מחשבה זו בשם רצון כלל,
phrases.en: this kind of *machshava* is not called *ratzon*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

phrases.en: because this is not taking place in these same nerves

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

phrases.en: it's happening in the left part of the brain, or whichever parts of the brain are the part of *bina*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

phrases.he: דהיינו בכלי ההשגה וההבנה של השכל עצמו,
phrases.en: this is the *kli* in the brain for the actual understanding and grasp of things

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

phrases.en: there's also the *kli* for this intellectual thought, this analytical thought

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

phrases.en: for every intellectual idea that is grasped

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

phrases.en: that happens in *Malchus d'Tevuna*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

phrases.he: דהיינו סוף מדריגת אור ההשגה בעצם המביא להשגה בענין הנבדל

phrases.en: like we've explained in chapter two, the *Malchus d'Tevuna* is the ability to take what you understand and express it in something separate from the understanding

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: This kind of *machshava* is not called *ratzon*, though the first kind is synonymous with it. It is only a thought process, not in the same nerves; it happens in the brain of *bina* itself.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: He has not looked at this in a while. The thought takes place in the gray matter of the cerebrum, where most thought happens.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: This is the *kli* in the brain for the actual understanding and grasp of things, and also for analytical thought and every intellectual grasp.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: *Malchus d'Tevuna* is the ability to take an idea and find symbolic representations for it, making associations. That is very similar to *Adam Kadmon*, also called *Adam d'Briah*, which corresponds to *bina*; the idea has to coin names or words for things.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: Once a person notices something important, he gives it a name or symbol. Thinking in a language means choosing words to be a *kli* for the idea; that happens in *Malchus d'Tevuna*, which, as explained in chapter two, takes what one understands and expresses it in something separate from the understanding.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

sections.title: Understanding comes before words; Leah is words without the mind
sections.summary: The light of understanding is first grasped without words, and the words come after. *Malchus d'Tevuna* is the level that puts an idea into words; *Leah* is words that are thought without the understanding behind them.

phrases.he: משם נעשה כח מחשבת שכל הנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: this is the source of this power to create intellectual thought

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

phrases.he: כי תחלה באה אור השגת השכל
phrases.en: because even in intellect, it begins as a subconscious process that doesn't have words

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

phrases.en: even the understanding itself, the actual analysis itself, originally happens without the *machshava*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

phrases.he: (הנקרא דער פאר נעמען אין פאר שטאנד אליין כו')
phrases.en: this is where it's just grasped, and a person understands something, first they understand it and then they're able to verbalize it to themselves and think about it

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: This is the source of the power to create intellectual thought. Even understanding begins as a subconscious process with no words, so the analysis itself happens first, without the *machshava*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: First a person grasps something, and only then verbalizes it and thinks about it: recognizing and noticing distinctions and patterns.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.title: Staring at a pattern
blocks.text: He thinks one sees this when staring at a grid. As a child he stared at the metal grating over a radiator, and his mind kept finding different patterns in it, one way and then another. Tiles and any very regular pattern do the same: the brain cuts them into patterns that are not really there. It is a subconscious process, and one can see its effect on the brain.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: That is *bina* itself, constantly looking for patterns and recognizing things.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: The brain is very good at finding faces. Even the headlights and grate of a car can look like a face, or the little knobs on a drawer. Faces are hardwired into us to help us recognize people and animals. People also find patterns in clouds and constellations, where there are only random dots.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.title: Movie sets and video games
blocks.text: There are two parts of reality, objective and subjective, like the sun and the moon: G-d created both, both are real, so our subjective perception is part of creation. The ability to see patterns is there because G-d put it into us. Like a movie set, where the lights and effects create an experience while the set is only a background and a warehouse. In a video game, bricks look like a wall and stop a character, but they are only pixels; the programming gives a feeling of solidity. G-d intentionally creates experiences for us, knowing how He made us. There is always an interplay between the two.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: The point is that our understanding and learning happen first, before conscious thought. Little children and animals learn before they can speak, in the pre-verbal part of us.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: Talking to ourselves and thinking consciously gives a huge advantage in learning: tools to think about ideas, organize them, and later share them by speaking. That is *machshava iyunis*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

phrases.he: טרם שחושב אור ההשכלה בלבוש דמחשבה ועיון עדיין,
phrases.en: before you think, you bring this light of the idea into the *levush* of *machshava* and *iyun*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

phrases.he: אך מיד מתפשט המושג והמושכל במחשבה עיונית
phrases.en: but right away that idea, which a person is thinking about, spreads out into this analytical thought

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: Before a person thinks it through, the light of understanding is not yet clothed in thought. Analytical thought tends to be a *levush*; the *machshava* of *ratzon* a *kli*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: Even within *sechel* there is an essential subconscious *machshava*, also a *kli*, as we discussed last time. Both aspects are on every level; generally *ratzon* is the *kli* and *sechel* the *levush*, since a symbol outside the essential experience is a *levush*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: Yet the idea, while still not thought out, spreads at once into analytical thought.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

phrases.en: and that's *Malchus d'Tevuna*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

phrases.he: שלמעלה מבחינת אותיות המחשבה שנקרא לאה
phrases.en: is higher than the letters of thought that are called *Leah*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: *Malchus d'Tevuna* is higher than the letters of thought, the ones called *Leah*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: When a person actively understands something, he creates new words for things, notices new distinctions, or coins new phrases. Someone writing a research paper, putting real new ideas into thought, is in *Malchus d'Tevuna*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: Words in the mind that are used to think, with little intellect going into them, like the lyrics of a song or thoughts about one's day, are called *Leah*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.title: Saying Shema without understanding
blocks.text: *Chovos HaLevavos*, in its Gate of Unity, speaks of this: many are trained to say *Shema Yisrael* and think 'there is one G-d' without understanding it. Those are letters of thought without the understanding, which is *Leah*, as opposed to *Malchus d'Tevuna*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

phrases.en: like it's known about in *Shema*, there's the large *dalet* of the word *Echad*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת מלכות דתבונה שמאחוריים דאימא כו',
phrases.en: which is the level of *Malchus d'Tevuna* that is behind *Imma*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

phrases.he: שמשם שרש התהוות המחשבה באותיות ממש כמו שכתוב במקום אחר)
phrases.en: that's the source of the letters of thought, where you create the symbols that give you language, as it is explained elsewhere

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: The large *dalet* of *Echad* in *Shema* stands for *Malchus*: letters in *Zeir Anpin* are large when they show their source in *Bina* and small when they show how they are in *Malchus*; the large *dalet* is the *Malchus d'Tevuna* behind *Imma*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: This is the source of the letters of thought, where the symbols that give us language are created; he explains it elsewhere. Here the aim is two types of thought, *ratzon* and the *machshava* of *sechel*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

phrases.he: ובחינת ההשכלה עצמה המושגת בהשגה והבנה גם כן נקרא מחשבה
phrases.en: and the actual idea that you understand itself, in *bina* itself, is also called thought

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: The idea that one understands, in *bina* itself, is also called *machshava*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

sections.title: Understanding has a depth that words cannot hold
sections.summary: *Chachma* is a direct experience, and *bina* turns it into distinctions and words. Inside *bina* there is a depth of the concept that no words can hold; it is also the essence of *Torah*, and understanding has to be plugged into experience to reach it.

phrases.en: but that is the experience

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

phrases.en: as that's the *yesh* of the light of *chachma*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

phrases.en: and that's called the *chashav mah*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

phrases.he: ויש בחינת פנימיות מחשבה דבינה דלא משתמע
phrases.en: and there is this inner thought of *bina* that is not heard

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

phrases.en: it's not able to be expressed and verbalized even in intellectual thought

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

phrases.en: you can't bring it into words

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: This is the experience of *chachma*, a direct experience, like the art example.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: A *machshava* of *chachma* experiences something like seeing with the mind's eye: looking into oneself, at the outside world, or at a G-dly thing, all are direct experiences in *chachma*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: The part of that experience one can begin to distinguish is sent to *bina*: the *yesh* of the light of *chachma*, called *chashav mah*, which is also how *machshava* is spelled.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: *Mah* is *bitul*: thinking about something abstract and *batel*. So the thought of *chachma* is *chashav mah*, when *bina* is receiving the letters of *chachma*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: That is pre-verbal, without words yet, like a person drawing who thinks about only the light and shadows. Any thinking has this kind of process.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: There is an inner thought of *bina* that is not heard, even in intellectual thought. It cannot be brought into words at all.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: Even within *sechel* the true depth of understanding cannot be explained, even to oneself. To make words one builds a caricature of the system: a few details given names, and 99.99 percent of what is really experienced and understood is left out.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: That is why you can't explain seeing red, tasting something, or loving somebody. The same holds for G-dliness: the *nefesh elokis* in a Jew, the holiness of *Torah u'Mitzvos*. Words can channel these things, but first you need openness to the direct experience.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.title: The color red
blocks.text: A word about the color red brings out the experience from one's memory. Without that experience, the words alone would not do it.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: In any understanding and any *hisbonenus*, the main thing is *emunah* and a direct experience higher than *sechel*, plugged into the *sechel*. Otherwise it is just words.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.title: Memorized formulas
blocks.text: People memorize words: kids memorize a math formula with no understanding of what it means or why it works, and would say the opposite if told it. Unfortunately, the same can happen with *Torah*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.title: The Rebbe's hearos
blocks.text: He thinks this is one reason the Rebbe encouraged *hearos*. At a *sicha* on Rashi he announced which Rashi, and encouraged questions, sometimes choosing one from the *bochurim*'s *hearos*, to train people to ask what the words mean.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: That is the difference between real meaning and mere reciting. One can learn *Shaar HaYichud* and think about the names of the levels with no understanding. It plugs into experience only when one first finds the ideas in oneself, which is why these *meshalim* are given, and then in *avodas Hashem*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

phrases.en: and this is the idea of the *omek hamusag*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

phrases.he: שלא נתפס גם בהשגה ומחשבה דבינה
phrases.en: the depth of understanding that cannot be expressed in the *otiyos* and in the thought

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

phrases.en: and that's like the essence of the *Torah*; the essence of the *Torah* is a G-dly appreciation of a G-dly holy thing that is beyond what you can codify in *Shulchan Aruch* and things like that

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: This is the *omek hamusag*, the *shaar hanun* of *bina*: the depth of understanding that cannot be expressed in letters or in thought.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: That depth is the essence of the *Torah*: a G-dly appreciation of a holy thing, beyond what can be codified in *Shulchan Aruch*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

sections.title: What cannot be asked: the inner Torah, the soul's experience and the mishkan
sections.summary: *Mi* is the part of *bina* that cannot be asked about, only experienced. The inner *Torah* and the G-dly soul are like this. Understanding does not create them; it builds a *mishkan* that lets them dwell in the everyday self.

phrases.en: there's a who that cannot be asked

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב במקום אחר) ודי למבין.
phrases.en: as explained elsewhere, and that's sufficed to understand

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: There is a *mi* that cannot be asked. You can ask about a person: what work he does, what he looks like. But who he really is cannot be asked; you have to meet the person, or be the person.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: So *mi* is like the level of *bina*: within *bina* a part can be asked about, and a part, *mi d'lo kayima lishaela*, must be experienced directly. Explained elsewhere; enough for the one who understands.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: Pausing to think about this: we have talked about what this is in ourselves.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: Plugging this in: the difference between *ratzon* and *sechel* is like *nigleh* and *nistar*. The *pnimiyus haTorah* is like the *machshava* of *ratzon*: what G-d wants, the spirit of the law, beyond expression even in the *halachos*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: One comes to recognize this through the fact that one has a soul which is a part of G-d.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: The recognition of the *pnimiyus* of the *Torah* is, he would say, the *Shechinah*: a person studying *Torah* with the awareness that it is holy and G-dly, which goes far beyond understanding something.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: That recognition is the real essence, the *Shechinah*. The codifiable part is the *nigleh*, a *levush* called *Metatron*, the angel of the *Torah*. We need the *neshamah* of the *Torah* plugged into its *guf*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: A similar thing appears in *Kuntres HaHispaalus*: the excitement of the natural soul, the *nefesh hateva*, comes from understanding logical things about a world of *yesh*, which is mainly the *machshava* of *sechel*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: The *nefesh elokis* comes from direct experience and feeling, not understanding: I'm a Jew, of course; there's *chametz* on Pesach. It is not even a question.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: *Hisbonenus* only helps tap into that and awaken it. With the animal soul, understanding creates the feelings, which is more external. We need both.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: In every *hisbonenus* we appreciate the created *yesh* we can understand, and the G-dly *ein* that creates it, beyond understanding: there we only have awe, humility, wonder and *bitul*, and cannot say we really know it.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: Everything has two sides. Some things we can measure and predict. But consciousness, the soul and life we connect to in the way of *makif*, *sovev kol almin*, and most of reality is created this way, through *ratzon*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: Some things are inherently transcendent, like meaning and purpose: we experience them directly, but they have no *kli* in the physical world where they live. So sometimes it says that *neshamos* are the idea of the letters of thought.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: Our *nefesh elokis* is like the *machshava* of G-d's *ratzon* and *taanug*; the *nefesh hateva* is the *machshava* of *sechel*. Our *yetzer tov* and *yetzer hara* are called angels.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: We have two kinds of experience: soul experiences beyond words, and things we can explain and measure. It is important to appreciate the strengths and limits of both and how they relate. That is a key thing.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.title: A yahrtzeit
blocks.text: Recently was a relative's *yahrtzeit*. He was thinking about various things, and suddenly had a very deep, very moving feeling of connection to that relative's *neshamah*. It is beyond what can be expressed in words or logic.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: The same can happen going to a holy place, or bringing a child for an *aliyah* for his bar mitzvah in the Rebbe's room, or preparing for a special *yom tov*. Such experiences can be very transcendent, and sometimes they are not.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: Sometimes we live only within our minds and logic: that is the difference between *bekol me'odecha* and *bekol levavecha*. They are parallel tracks of reality and experience, and both must be understood.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: Our *avodah*: connect to the higher thing, the letters of *ratzon*, our *nefesh elokis*, *emunah* and *mesiras nefesh*; then use the understanding of *bina* as a *kli* to plug that in, bringing them into the *pnimiyus*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: Building a *mishkan* for the *Shechinah*: we have the connection, but need a *mishkan* so it is present in our *nefesh habehamis* or *nefesh hateva* as something reliable, not only in moments of inspiration.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: Sometimes understanding must come first, to help a person reach that experience; that is where *Chassidus* has two sides too.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.title: The Alter Rebbe's mask
blocks.text: After the Alter Rebbe came out of Petersburg, like Moshe coming down from the second *luchos* with his face shining, he would sometimes wear a mask: off for *Bnei Yisroel*, on for the *erev rav*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

sensitivity.reason: Names the erev rav, the group the Alter Rebbe would speak to with the mask on. A classical term from the story, not his own remark on people.
sensitivity.judgmentNote: The erev rav is the story's own term for the mixed multitude; decide whether it prints as said or as the plainer words in publishable.
sensitivity.publishable: After the Alter Rebbe came out of Petersburg, like Moshe coming down from the second *luchos* with his face shining, he would sometimes wear a mask: off for *Bnei Yisroel*, on for the mixed multitude.

blocks.text: The mask is the *haskala* of *Chassidus*. Its essence is the G-dliness in it, beyond human intellect: a G-dly understanding. The *Frierdiker Rebbe* has a beautiful talk on this in *Likutei Dibburim*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: Sometimes you need the mask to get the *nefesh hateva* ready to unlock, and refined enough for the *Shaar HaNun*, the essence of the *Torah*: the *sefiras ha'omer*, refining ourselves to that experience, a gift from G-d.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: G-d gives us a *nefesh elokis* higher than logic. Recognizing it, we bring that experience into understanding: that is the proper way of learning *Torah* and doing *avodah*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: First a person refines himself enough to get in touch with his soul. Then the *avodah* is to make *kelim* to express it; making a *kli* for what is higher than understanding is very different.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.title: Color and a rose
blocks.text: Two people who have seen a color can talk about it, because they share the essential experience. A rose given to show love is a symbol of something infinite, if both recognize it is much higher than a physical exchange; as a bribe, it is very different.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: That is what art is in general: trying to capture things beyond ordinary words and expression, and finding ways to express them, with the recognition that one is connecting to something deeper. That is bringing *ruchniyus* into *gashmiyus* and making a *mishkan* for it.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

blocks.text: He will return to this at the end of the chapter: the *otiyos* of *ratzon* later come into and are expressed in *sechel*. They start out separate and are supposed to become fused.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.1 ehanced.mp3

sections.title: Both kinds of thought run through every level, and both come from the essence of the soul
sections.summary: The thought of *ratzon* and the thought of *bina* run through every level of the *seder hishtalshelus*. Both come from the essence of the soul, which is also the source of the letters of thought.

phrases.en: There's the thought of desire, which is subconscious

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: and then there's the verbal thought of *bina*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: הבאה לכלל בחינת אותיות דמחשבה ממש, שנקרא לאה
phrases.en: which is expressed in actual letters of language, which is called *Leah*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: כו' וכל זה יש גם ברצון שלמעלה מן השכל
phrases.en: So all of these, this relationship of these two types of *ratzon*, exists in every level, even in the *ratzon* that's higher than *sechel*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: This is what the *Zohar* says: two types of thought, the subconscious thought of *ratzon*, and the analytical thought of *bina*, which is expressed in actual letters and is called *Leah*. Through this process the analytical thought eventually creates the language itself.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: This relationship between the two types of thought also exists on every level, even in the *ratzon* higher than *sechel*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: דאריך אנפין, שהוא בחינת מחשבה נעלמת ברצון הנעלם,
phrases.en: there's the subconscious *bina* of *Keser*, of *Arich Anpin*, which is a *machshava* within the subconscious *ratzon*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: כמו שיש שכל וחכמה דאריך אנפין הנעלם
phrases.en: just like there is the *chachma* that's hidden

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: מכל רעיון הנעלם, והוא בחינת חכמה סתימאה דאריך אנפין הנקרא טעם כמוס לרצון כידוע, כך יש בחינת בינה סתימאה כו')
phrases.en: the subconscious *chachma*, which is called *chachma stimaah*, and there's also *bina stimaah*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: והוא על דרך מה שאנו רואים ההפרש בין ב' מיני מחשבות הנזכר לעיל בגלוי
phrases.en: and this is like we see, between these two types of thoughts

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: שהוא ברצון הבא בגלוי במוח, שיש רצון שבגידי המוח, שנקרא מחשבה סתימאה על שם ההעלם של זה הרצון שבמוח טרם שבא לחכמה ובינה כו'

blocks.text: This is the subconscious *bina* of *Keser*, of *Arich Anpin*: a *machshava* within the subconscious *ratzon*. Just as there is a hidden *chachma* that is called *chachma stimaah*, there is also a *bina stimaah*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The same is true in *Keser* of *Atzilus*, *Adam Kadmon*, or any of these levels: even within the *ratzon* there are two aspects.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: A thought expressed simply as how I want to feel is an extension of the self; it becomes associated with something separate, as with the *igulim* and *yosher*. This happens on every level of the *seder hishtalshelus*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: *Machshava* has two aspects, a *kli* and a *levush*. The essential thought is the *kli*; the *bina* aspect creates the *levush*, which attaches to something non-essential, what philosophy calls circumstantials, things that could change.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: There is a choice to express it in one way, though it could have been expressed in infinite ways. G-d chose to make the ten *sefiros*, each with a certain form; so within the Jewish people there is our *neshamah* and *guf*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The *neshamah* is essential, the *guf* more external; like the *pnimiyus haTorah* and the *nigleh shel Torah*, with all kinds of aspects.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: This is like what we see in the revealed: the difference between the two types of thought mentioned above.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The desire expressed in the mind is also in the nerves of the brain, which is called subconscious thought, named for the hiddenness of the desire before it reaches *chachma* and *bina*. When a person walks or moves, the desire is expressed in the body's nerves, not verbally.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: A person is not necessarily aware of thinking 'lift my foot', or of breathing. The autonomic nervous system pumps the heart and makes the lungs breathe. We can consciously move and breathe, but even that is not necessarily verbal: we choose to do it.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Things become more conscious until they become actual symbols and thought. All of this comes before *chachma* and *bina*, when there is just the *machshava* of *ratzon*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: And then there's the intellectual thought, the analytical thought

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: that is when the *ayin* of *chachma*, that concept, is being expressed in some sort of tangible way, where we create symbols for it and we create a structure for it

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: עד שבא לכלל אותיות דמחשבה ממש
phrases.en: until it becomes actual verbal thought

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Analytical thought is the *yesh* of *chachma*: the *ayin* of *chachma* expressed tangibly, with symbols and a structure, until it becomes actual verbal thought.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Subconscious thought has a similar process in the higher self, and the *seder hishtalshelus* has it on every level, back before the *tzimtzum*. He will say more. Now a parenthesis.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: and based on what was explained previously in chapter 38

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: בשרש הראשון של האותיות דמחשבה בעצם הנפש ממש,
phrases.en: about how the source of the letters of thought, even though they seem external, but they actually come from the *etzem*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: הרי יש שרש לאותיות המחשבה דבינה גם כן בעצם הנפש
phrases.en: part of the essence of the soul

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Based on chapter 38: the source of the first letters of thought is in the essence of the soul. They seem external, but come from the *etzem*, through choices from the essence of the soul; so too the letters of *bina*'s thought.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Every desire expresses a flavor of my essence, and so does the way I frame and understand the world: that too is a direct choice and expression of the essence.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: A kind of theory of relativity: the world has no preferred reference point or logical system, so I can impose any system on it. Like language, it does not matter if you name something in English, Hebrew, French or Portuguese.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: When I view the world a certain way, through a certain framework or words, I project it onto the world: a choice from the essence of the soul.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: just like there is the source for the letters of *ratzon* that are subconscious, that are in the nerves

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: come from the *Atzmus* of the soul, so, too, these different symbols that we create for verbal thought also come from the essence of the soul

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The printed text says lights; a footnote says other editions read *shoresh* (source), which he thinks is the more likely reading.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The source of the subconscious letters of *ratzon*, in the nerves, is the *Atzmus* of the soul; so too these symbols for verbal thought come from the essence of the soul.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: רק שזה בא לבחינת גלוי לרצון,
phrases.en: just that one type of letters is coming from the soul to be the revelation of desire

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: וזה בא לבחינת גלוי אותיות דבינה
phrases.en: and one is coming from the essence of the soul to be the expression for the letters of understanding of *bina*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: to understand an intellectual concept

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: One kind of letters comes from the soul to reveal desire; the other, from the essence of the soul, expresses the letters of *bina* that grasp an intellectual concept.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Both levels of letters come from the essence of the soul; in the *nimshal*, both come from G-d's *Atzmus* and directly express His choice.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

sections.title: Desire shapes understanding: the chosen nature, the revelation of Keser in Bina
sections.summary: What is desired is the essential nature a Jew has, which the mind is to take up and express, with the *avodah* of making *kelim* for it. The last parts of the chapter show the same pattern in the revelation of *Keser* in *Bina*, the *Atik* in *Bina*, and the three points of the letter yud.

phrases.he: ואמנם הרי אנו רואים דמה שעולה ברצונו ומחשבתו הוא אשר בא עד בחינת אותיות המחשבה דבינה,
שנמשך בחינת הרצון ומחשבה הנעלם במחשבה הגלויה דבינה)
phrases.en: But there's also another relationship, that we see that a person's desire, the letters that come up and what's expressed in a person's desire in that kind of subconscious thought, that makes its way and is expressed, and influences and colors the way that the person thinks in the thought, the letters of *bina*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Another relationship: a person's desire, and the letters that arise in it, make their way into his thought and color the way he thinks, which is the letters of *bina*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: A person names things by what is important to him: language is shaped by desire, so we create words for the distinctions that matter to us. Even our logic is ultimately an expression of desire.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: This is expressed in the Rebbe's *ma'amar* that he said for 11 Nissan.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.title: The king and his officers
blocks.text: The midrash: a king came with his generals and dukes, and everyone invited the officers, hoping to gain by befriending them. One wise person said he would invite the king himself.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The reasons for choosing the king are many, but really it is a deeper choice. G-d chooses us and gives us a nature; with a G-dly soul we connect to the *pnimiyus* of *ratzon*, and prefer the inner essence to an external connection.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The Rebbe explains that this connection is expressed in our essential nature from G-d: a Jew can never be separated from G-d, and does not want to be, *nisht er ken, nisht er vil zayn nifrad*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Our essential nature is the *otiyos* of *ratzon* and *taanug*. Brought into understanding, with reasons for choosing this way, it is a creative expression of our choice to personalize our connection to G-d.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: One of the big *klalim* of *Chassidus*: we take our *emunah*, though we have the essential connection, and personalize it by bringing it into understanding.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Bringing it into *Torah* and *hisbonenus* means finding *kelim* to express it. They are more external, yet an expression of the essence too; that is very important.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The source of the letters of *machshava* and *dibbur* is in the essence of the soul, so it is higher. In *Shaarei Orah* he says that a person who refines his *middos* has made that change, but the memories of what he thought and did stay connected to the essence of the soul.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: So a separate *avodah* has to happen, the *avodas hakatores*, to rectify those letters: set aside hours saying or thinking the words of *Torah*, as *Hayom Yom* says, and saying things by heart.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Saying much *Tehillim* and *Mishnayos* by heart is connecting our letters to something. Wanting G-dliness, being a Jew in one's heart, is not enough; we need to express it.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: That is part of why we have so many *mitzvos*, *lezakos es Yisroel*, to bring us merit. We should always be thinking of G-dliness and plugging it in different ways.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The relationship is true in higher levels, as in *kamayim hapanim lapanim*. Our *avodah* causes an *isoruso d'letata*, which causes an *isoruso d'lelo*: measure for measure, *midah keneged midah*. This comes from the essence, even the light before the *tzimtzum*, the original desire of *chafetz chesed*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.title: Should I create the world?
blocks.text: First there was the desire that G-d desired kindness. He consulted the *neshamos hatzadikim*: should I create the world? When they said yes, the plan, *Ana Emloch*, the level of *Kadmon*, planned the whole *seder hishtalshelus*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The desire for creation is a projection from us: G-d looks toward our *neshamos*. Though they are more external, like the letters of *machshava*, we are rooted higher than the original *ratzon*, so in a way we are its source.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Simply put: everything in the *seder hishtalshelus* is created for us and for our *avodah*, the ultimate source. Though we seem to be creation and lower, everything is really for that.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: This goes to *igulim* and *yosher*, or *tikkun* and *tohu*. The *pnimiyus* is the main thing in one way; in another the *ma'aseh* and its outward expression are. It could have come out many ways; that G-d chose the Jewish people and gave us a body and *Torah u'Mitzvos* is an expression of the essence.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.title: The lot of Purim
blocks.text: We should see this even deeper than the simplicity of the *Ein Sof*, that it could have been any way. That goes also to *Purim* and the *goral*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: this is the idea of *Ehyeh asher Ehyeh*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: G-d told *Moshe* to tell the Jewish people, "I will be what I will be"

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: דאריך אנפין בכתר הפרטי שהוא בבינה
phrases.en: this is the idea that the general *keser*, right, *ehyeh* means "I will be", in other words an expression of the self

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: *Ehyeh asher Ehyeh*: G-d told *Moshe* to say, 'I will be what I will be.' The first *ehyeh* is *Keser*, the second *Bina*: the general *Keser* of *Arich Anpin* revealed in the particular *Keser* in *Bina*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The general *Keser*: *ehyeh* means 'I will be', an expression of the self. That self is expressed in *Keser*, and more externally in *Bina*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: G-d's essential nature is plugged into how He creates the world, chooses the Jewish people, and gives us the *Torah*, and all these kinds of things.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: וכידוע ומבואר במקום אחר בענין ועבד הלוי הוא,
phrases.en: and this is explained elsewhere about this, that the *Levi* is like serving the *Keser*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: that *Atik*, which is the *pnimiyus* of *Keser*, or the essence, or the *yechida*, that is expressed specifically in *bina*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The *Levi* is like serving the *Keser*, as explained elsewhere. *Atik Yomin* is revealed specifically in *Bina*: *Atik*, the *pnimiyus* of *Keser*, the essence or *yechida*, also in *Chachma*, more externally.

blocks.text: We have *emunah*, or a *neshamah*, simply because we are born that way, like children to G-d. That is our essential nature, more external than our choosing G-d.

blocks.text: This is the idea of the three horns of the letter *yud*. It is a little hard to explain without a picture.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: In a printed *siddur*, or in this book, the *yud* usually looks as if it has two horns: a horn up at the top left, and a little point at the bottom right.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: In a *Sefer Torah* the *yud* is a line: from the top left point it goes straight down, with a thicker stroke from the middle to a point at the bottom right. So there is a third point, directly below the top left.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The top left point is the source of *chachma* in *Keser*; the point directly below it is the *yesod* of *chachma*, the revelation of *Keser* in the flash of *chachma*, and of *emunah*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 40/040 Shaar HaYichud ch 40.2 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: From there it goes right and comes down into *bina*: how *Keser* and *chachma* come down into understanding, lower in one way, is actually higher; the *Shaar HaNun* of *bina* reaches the *Atzmus* more than *chachma* does.
